clue.text: Humdrum allotments in which funds may be invested

definitions.text: in which funds may be invested

parts.note: something humdrum is commonplace, run-of-the-mill
allotments are portions handed out, as stock is apportioned to investors

explanation.surface: Dull garden plots are recommended as a home for investment money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotments' suggests British garden plots rented from the council, but here it means portions allotted, as stock is.
explanation.definitionFit: Common stock in a company is a standard vehicle for investors' money.

clue.text: Sends away for instructions?

explanation.surface: Someone posting off a request for directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To send away for goods is to request them by mail; commands given are also directives of that name.

clue.text: Array of pods or flags

indicators.note: to array things is to set them out in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between a display of seed pods or a row of banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Array of' shuffles PODS and OR together; 'flags' is the verb, wilts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flags is wilting and sagging, losing its vigour.

clue.text: Rugger player brought up on the Meuse

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it upside down, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union, the game called rugger
a man is a player in a team or a piece in a board game

explanation.surface: A rugby player raised beside a Belgian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses RUMAN in this down clue. Namur is a Belgian city where the Sambre joins the Meuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian city stands on that river at its confluence with the Sambre.

clue.text: Withdraw what has been said about a religious treatise

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning
a tract is a short pamphlet, often on a religious subject

explanation.surface: Taking back one's comments on a theological pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is to recant it.

clue.text: See 1
Supporting or obstructing attack?

explanation.surface: A tactic that both props up and blocks an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Propping something aloft is bearing it up; a stick-up or delay of an assault is also this phrase, as in a robbery or traffic jam.

clue.text: Rule broken by a stupid fellow meaning to make a fresh allocation

indicators.note: the first word is split open so another can sit in the gap

parts.note: to rule is to reign, and a reign is a period of rule
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Government disrupted by a fool who intends to hand out jobs again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' signals a container; 'meaning to' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot something anew is to give it out a second time to a different holder.

clue.text: Stops working for a time?

parts.note: a halt that is only temporary, as a business, a bus service or a share's trading may be paused

explanation.surface: A machine that keeps cutting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a faulty device; the sense is halting something temporarily, as trading in a share is halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt an activity temporarily is to put it in abeyance.

clue.text: Downtrodden shoe-cleaners

parts.note: mats at the entrance are literally trodden on as boots are wiped, and people who are put upon are given the same name

explanation.surface: Oppressed bootblacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downtrodden' is literal for the mats under foot and figurative for meek people.
explanation.definitionFit: Mats at the threshold clean shoes and are walked on; meek people treated as such are also called by the name.

clue.text: Complaints that may come from fold or stable

indicators.note: the answer is said to come out of the word stable, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Grumbles heard from the sheep pen or the stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: A fold is a sheep pen, so bleating does come from it; the stable supplies the letters, which 'may come from' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble whining moans resemble the cry of a sheep or goat.

clue.text: Mistakenly keep a pampered pet, maybe

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order, as if by mistake

explanation.surface: Wrongly owning a spoilt animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistakenly' rearranges KEEP. A Pekingese is a lapdog famous for being spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small lapdog, the classic cosseted pooch.

clue.text: Writing in the papers about fortified wine and what may improve it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
port is a fortified wine from Portugal
port gets better with age as it matures in the bottle

explanation.surface: Newspaper copy on port and how it matures.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic accounts of events are news reporting.

clue.text: The children Susan is heading

indicators.note: the first word goes in front, at the head of the second in this across clue

parts.note: Sue is a short form of the name Susan

explanation.surface: Susan is leading the youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' looks like Susan leading the children, but it puts one piece on top of the other; 'The children' is the definition, in its legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language one's offspring are one's descendants, as in 'died without issue'.

clue.text: Unable to move quickly

explanation.surface: Stuck and yet speedy, a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck fast means immovably fixed; to run fast is to run rapidly.

clue.text: Celt with an eye disorder easily made light of

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Celt whose eye condition was dismissed lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' shuffles CELT and AN EYE. 'Made light of' looks like dismissing something, but the gas is what light is easily made of, in old lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas burns with a bright flame and was used in miners' and bicycle lamps.

clue.text: Not free to marry?

parts.note: someone betrothed is already spoken for, though the reading also covers a phone line or toilet in use

explanation.surface: Someone tied down and unable to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means busy as well as betrothed, and the betrothed are in a sense free to marry, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being betrothed means already promised to someone, and occupied in general.

clue.text: Quietly going ahead and addressing the court?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
leading is being out in front

explanation.surface: A barrister quietly proceeds to speak to the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer making a case to a judge argues it, which is what pleaders do.

clue.text: I first leave and see about returning

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'I first leave and see about returning', has no definition, and its wordplay builds E+QUITI+ES only if 'I' follows QUIT, which 'first' contradicts; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: I first leave and see about returning

clue.text: A drink that's short and sweet

definitions.text: A drink that's short and sweet

parts.words: A drink that's short and sweet
parts.note: the phrase 'short and sweet' means brief, but here a short is a small strong drink, and this one is sugary

explanation.surface: Something brief and pleasant, a familiar phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: A short is a small measure of spirits; these after-dinner drinks are sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet flavoured spirit served in small glasses after dinner.

clue.text: One way to secure a string of pearls, perhaps

explanation.surface: Fastening a necklace safely.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord ties things down; a long necklace of pearls is also called a cord of that name.

clue.text: An out-of-step Irish division :

indicators.note: a word put out of place has its letters disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish unit marching out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of' (from out-of-step) rearranges STEP. A sept is a clan or branch of a family in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish clan or branch of a family goes by this name.

clue.text: Gretel's version of a classic event

indicators.note: a new version of a word is its letters rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Gretel's own account of a famous occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges GRETELS. The St Leger is a horse race at Doncaster, one of the five English Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: This Doncaster horse race is one of the five Classics of English flat racing.

clue.text: Sit up and beg for an ersatz handkerchief

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or plead, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: A dog performing tricks for a fake hankie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals reversal in a down clue; the surface pictures a dog's trick, and 'sit up and beg' is a familiar command.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper hankie is a substitute for the cloth one.

clue.text: They are privately said to pass on information

definitions.text: They are privately said to pass on information

parts.words: They are privately said to pass on information
parts.note: remarks muttered out of others' hearing, as by actors to the audience, which convey extra knowledge

explanation.surface: Gossips whispering secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks spoken so only some can hear are muttered confidences, often theatrical.

clue.text: It may develop into friendship

indicators.note: the letters grow into a new form, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A relationship that could blossom into friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop into' rearranges IT MAY; 'may' looks like a modal verb but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful goodwill between people or nations is friendly harmony.

clue.text: In bygone days their occupants stood to get a lot of abuse from the public

definitions.text: In bygone days their occupants stood to get a lot of abuse from the public

parts.words: In bygone days their occupants stood to get a lot of abuse from the public
parts.note: the wooden frames that held an offender's head and hands for crowds to pelt and jeer

explanation.surface: People in times past who faced public ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood to get' reads as 'were likely to get', but the occupants literally stood in these frames.
explanation.definitionFit: The old wooden frame with holes for head and hands exposed offenders to public scorn.

clue.text: A beast that is spotted and endlessly enounced?

indicators.note: read as without END: the letters E, N and D are taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: A spotted animal whose name is declared incompletely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the letters E, N, D (in that order) from ENOUNCED. The beast is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a spotted big cat of Central Asia, has this other name.

clue.text: I'm about to stay in the same place, literally

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second, about meaning surrounding

parts.note: the contraction I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will remain where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container. 'Literally' means in literature: this Latin word is used in footnotes and citations.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin footnote term refers to the work just cited, meaning the same source.

clue.text: Full of anguish, Ida's gone astray

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of place and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with the s counted
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ida has wandered off and someone is distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges IDAS and GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in torment is suffering great pain or distress.

clue.text: He's after fuel cuts in a big way

indicators.note: the second word follows, coming after the first in this across clue

parts.note: gas is a fuel
the contraction he's gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man looking for petrol, with big reductions involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the order of the two pieces; 'cuts' suggests price reductions but means deep wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep, long wounds are severe slashes.

clue.text: Like the prairie fish caught in a lock, apparently

indicators.note: one word is trapped inside another

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish snagged in a canal lock, by the look of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' signals a container. 'Lock' suggests a canal but is hair; 'apparently' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie is grassland without woods.
